goal: Find the cancellation age window for subscriber winback messages.
whyThisDefault: The age window preserves the established outreach timing after cancellation. The platform keeps its neutral default of requiring retention consent at the send gate.

frozenOn: Existing winback delivery receipts retain their deduplication identity.

runtime.reason: Discovery documents the age window and send gate. The full policy and episode changes need separate qualification.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Set the minimum base unit count required when editing a classic subscription (minimum base units, subscription edit floor, package minimum).

absentMeans.description: Both TypeScript (createPostgresPackageEditReadPort) and SQL subscription edit paths fail closed with subscription_reprice_minimum_base_units_unavailable when no valid positive 32-bit integer is stored in commerce_settings.value_text.

whyThisDefault: The platform provides no implicit floor for classic subscription edits; stores must explicitly install a positive 32-bit integer row in commerce_settings.

effect.appliesTo: Classic subscription edit quotes and SQL applies read the installed minimum base-unit count from commerce_settings.value_text; host edit admission checks for drift against configured offer minimums before admitting edits.
frozenOn: Existing active subscriptions and already completed edit command receipts retain their agreed quantities and prices.

runtime.reason: Install or update the commerce_settings row through your store installation step; host edit admission refuses drift against application configuration.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Set the introductory fixed-cycle and graduation-cycle boundaries for sized subscription editing (intro phase, graduation cycle, starter pack editing).

absentMeans.description: Introductory starter-pack subscriptions fail closed in SQL with subscription_edit_invalid_sized_configuration when no valid JSON row is installed in commerce_settings.value_text. In the starter, owned/subscription-editing.ts holds the code copy while owned/demo-seed.ts installs the matching database copy; keep both aligned.

whyThisDefault: The platform provides no implicit introductory phase cutoff; stores must explicitly install fixedThroughCycle and graduationCycle in commerce_settings when introductory subscriptions use sized editing.

effect.appliesTo: Sized subscription edit commands for introductory starter-pack subscriptions evaluate fixedThroughCycle and graduationCycle from the installed commerce_settings row in SQL alongside the configured SizedEditPolicy in TypeScript (in the starter, keep owned/subscription-editing.ts aligned with the database row seeded by owned/demo-seed.ts).
frozenOn: Already completed edit command receipts and past paid cycles retain their recorded state.

runtime.reason: Install or update the commerce_settings row together with the application's SizedEditPolicy configuration.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Reprice renewal shipping from the current address.

runtime.reason: Retained native terms carry one shipping threshold profile.

goal: Customize renewal execution input, failure classification, and post-renewal or exhaustion outcome handling (after renewal, renewal policy, dunning exhaustion, failure classification).
whyThisDefault: The platform supplies neutral failure-key defaults via createDefaultRenewalFailurePolicy and leaves post-exhaustion actions unconfigured so hosts compose AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy from @openlup/platform/subscriptions explicitly.

effect.appliesTo: Subsequent renewal runs and failure-handling passes invoke the bound AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy callbacks from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.
frozenOn: Already recorded renewal operations, retry obligations, dunning cases, and completed command receipts retain their persisted state.

runtime.reason: The policy hooks are executable server code implementing AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Renew subscriptions on a fixed calendar day.

runtime.reason: Native cadence is expressed in days.

goal: Offer custom subscription pause durations.

runtime.reason: Native lifecycle commands support two weeks, one month and indefinite.

goal: Require delivery evidence and move alignment only later.

runtime.reason: A late delivery extends the cycle without stacking deliveries. A replacement counts only after arrival.

goal: Admit or refuse proposed subscription lines, quantities, and cadences before pricing a subscription edit (edit terms admission, offer admission, cadence validation).
whyThisDefault: Omitting admitSubscriptionTerms (SubscriptionTermsAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) preserves native subscription editing behavior with no application-specific offer filter beyond platform minimums and representation bounds.

effect.appliesTo: Fresh subscription edit previews and applies invoke the bound SubscriptionTermsAdmission callback (admitSubscriptionTerms from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) after normalization and before pricing or quote persistence.
frozenOn: Active subscription terms and already completed matching command receipts replay without re-evaluating changed admission rules.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SubscriptionTermsAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Schedule introductory discounts by renewal cycle.

runtime.reason: Native terms support one introductory phase before the retained terms take over.

goal: Admit or refuse fresh customer subscription lifecycle commands such as skip, slide, pause, resume, cancel, order_now, and reactivate (command admission, pause presets, account actions).
whyThisDefault: Omitting admitSubscriptionCommand (SubscriptionCommandAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) preserves native command behavior across all supported lifecycle actions subject to platform state and payment fences.

effect.appliesTo: Fresh subscription lifecycle previews and commands invoke the bound SubscriptionCommandAdmission callback (admitSubscriptionCommand from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) after replay checks and before durable writes.
frozenOn: Completed command receipts and existing pauses or cycle dates replay and retain their stored outcomes.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SubscriptionCommandAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Prepay several subscription deliveries.

runtime.reason: Native commands refuse multi-cycle prepaid subscriptions.

goal: Change a renewal price without changing the subscription basket.

runtime.reason: Native renewal prices are locked until an edit changes the terms.

goal: Calculate a subscription reschedule date in the market time zone.

runtime.reason: The native command compares dates using UTC days.

goal: Use one retry schedule for host and provider-recorded payment failures.

runtime.reason: Provider-recorded failures still use the fixed 24, 72 and 168 hour schedule.

goal: Use the same delivery controls for managed and native notices.

runtime.reason: Managed and native delivery paths use separate controls.

goal: Compute target variant quantities from daily need, cadence, and portion factor during sized subscription portion changes (portion proposal, resize bundle, sized editor).
whyThisDefault: The platform provides no default demand-to-quantity sizing formula; hosts supply SizedHostPorts.proposePortion from @openlup/platform/subscriptions, or refuse demand-driven resizing when unconfigured.

effect.appliesTo: New sized subscription portion-mode edits invoke SizedHostPorts.proposePortion from @openlup/platform/subscriptions before quoting and persisting updated lines.
frozenOn: Existing subscriptions and completed edit receipts retain their agreed lines and prices until a new edit is applied.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SizedHostPorts.proposePortion from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Set the stock hold lifetime when a renewal leaves stock wait.

runtime.reason: Native stock-wait recovery fixes the hold at 15 minutes in SQL. The separate reservation port reads holdSeconds from its own reserve call, outside native stock-wait recovery. The starter's scheduled renewal uses this port to expire reservations and leaves its holdSeconds option unused.

goal: Set windows for subscriber review requests.

runtime.reason: Review branches exist in SQL and need composition before exposing a setting.

goal: Reconcile unknown payment outcomes before retrying and stop on hard declines.

runtime.reason: Retrying a charge with an unknown outcome risks charging twice.

goal: Send winback again for a new cancellation episode.

runtime.reason: The native winback receipt deduplicates by subscription.
